name: flow-diagram
purpose: FlowDiagram renders a directed flow diagram: a horizontal sequence of steps (`flow-diagram-node`) joined by decorative connectors, with optional parallel branches (`flow-diagram-parallel`) and custom connector-attachment points (`flow-diagram-anchor`). Use it to visualize pipelines, workflows, and step-by-step processes inside a data view; unlike `table` it expresses ordered/branching relationships rather than tabular records. Steps are written as direct children of `flow-diagram`; a `flow-diagram-parallel` between two steps fans out from the previous step and fans back into the next, and a `flow-diagram-parallel` at the start/end fans only inward/outward (no dangling stubs). A node can be styled (the default box) or `unstyled` so its slot content defines the entire node — a dot, a tall card, a multi-row card — while connectors still attach correctly, optionally at `flow-diagram-anchor` points inside the node. Connectors run port-to-port: a styled node renders a small square **connector port** just outside each of its edges, and a `flow-diagram-anchor` renders one outside the edge it attaches to, so a line always terminates on a visible attachment point instead of a bare edge (the port is the endpoint treatment — connectors carry no arrowheads). The port sits fully clear of the box rather than overlapping it, so neither the node's surface nor its focus ring crops it. A port is only rendered where a connector actually attaches: the leading child has no incoming connector and the trailing child no outgoing one, so those two edges show no port and the chain opens and closes on a node rather than on a stub. An `unstyled` node renders no ports, because its slot content owns its appearance; put a `flow-diagram-anchor` inside it to place ports on the parts a connector should touch. Design source (rewritten to our conventions, never inherited as-is): the kumo "Flow" component group at https://kumo-ui.com/components/flow-diagram/. Scope boundary: large diagrams pan via a native `overflow: auto` scroll container on the root — free 2D drag-pan is intentionally out of scope (it would require an external positioning library forbidden by `.claude/rules/dependencies.md`). The connector port is specified by the Figma frame in the frontmatter; the remaining tokens are inferred from intent and recorded in the Theme gaps table.
useWhen: Showing an ordered pipeline or request path as steps joined by connectors — build → deploy → serve, or a request through a load balancer, a function and its bindings.
A step fans out to several parallel targets and (optionally) back in — wrap those steps in `FlowDiagram.Parallel`.
A node with custom content (a card with several rows) where connectors must touch specific parts — mark them with `FlowDiagram.Anchor`.
avoidWhen: One of the official architecture drawings, or a node-and-connector picture for a marketing page → use `diagram`.
Tabular records with no ordering between them → use `table`.
A numbered set of instructions in documentation → use `doc-steps`.
related: diagram` — marketing architecture drawings from a closed library or a one-off spec; `flow-diagram` is the in-product, hand-composed pipeline.
doc-steps` — an ordered walkthrough of text steps joined by a rail, not connected nodes.
table` — records without ordered or branching relationships.
bestPractices: Write steps as direct children of `FlowDiagram` in flow order; connectors are drawn between siblings, so wrapping nodes in extra elements breaks the chain.

Use `unstyled` when the slot content is the whole node, and put a `FlowDiagram.Anchor` (`side="end"` incoming, `side="start"` outgoing) on each part a connector should touch — an unstyled node renders no ports of its own.
Mark a leaf that hangs off the chain with `terminal`; it receives a connector but sends none on.
Do not clip a node with `overflow-hidden` in a wrapping card — the connector ports sit outside the node's box and would disappear.
Let a wide flow scroll in its own container; the root is an `overflow: auto` region, and there is no drag-to-pan.

props.name: align
props.doc: Vertical alignment of nodes within the diagram.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Diagram content: `flow-diagram-node` and `flow-diagram-parallel`, in flow order.

examples.name: Parallel
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import FlowDiagram from '@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram'
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram align="center">
    <FlowDiagram.Node>Start</FlowDiagram.Node>
    <FlowDiagram.Parallel>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Branch A</FlowDiagram.Node>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Branch B</FlowDiagram.Node>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Branch C</FlowDiagram.Node>
    </FlowDiagram.Parallel>
    <FlowDiagram.Node>End</FlowDiagram.Node>
  </FlowDiagram>
</template>

examples.name: Branches
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import FlowDiagram from '@aziontech/webkit/flow-diagram'
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram align="center">
    <FlowDiagram.Parallel>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>HTTP Trigger</FlowDiagram.Node>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Cron Trigger</FlowDiagram.Node>
    </FlowDiagram.Parallel>
    <FlowDiagram.Node>Process Request</FlowDiagram.Node>
    <FlowDiagram.Parallel>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Log Analytics</FlowDiagram.Node>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Update Cache</FlowDiagram.Node>
      <FlowDiagram.Node>Send Notification</FlowDiagram.Node>
    </FlowDiagram.Parallel>
    <FlowDiagram.Node>Complete</FlowDiagram.Node>
  </FlowDiagram>
</template>
